test_summary:
Task 3 Astra repair 3 completed in /home/ingmar/worktrees/ptest/cx-ng-product/task-3. Edited only src/ptest/history.py, tests/ng/test_history.py, and this report; preserved the pre-existing uncommitted repairs and reports. No commit, integration, global install, push, deployment, or controller-chain edit.

Repairs: actual SQLITE_FULL triggers deterministic growing batches of ordinary runs ordered by sequence/run_id, followed by reconciliation rows, with compact/retry bounded by the finite candidate set. Baseline and failure/whole-gate obligations are never evicted. Interrupted pruning reports coordinator-unavailable without falsely claiming exhaustion and retains the earlier capacity uncertainty. The protected-only fixture contains exactly one baseline summary before the failed publication. A real SQLite max_page_count test observes SQLITE_FULL and subsequent committed recovery; another test forces FULL until the oldest ordinary row is actually absent.

Capacity uncertainty: a private history-capacity.json with the exact version/code/sequence allowlist is reserved before modifying publication evidence. FULL therefore leaves visible uncertainty without needing another filesystem allocation; no sensitive values are stored. The record is distinct from permanent corruption, and existing uncertainty clears only after a newer validated clean full publication with conclusive passing outcomes. Scoped, older, and skipped recovery attempts cannot clear it. Transient failures restore the pre-call state. A bounded, private advisory writer lock serializes pruning/compaction/retry and marker transitions; a forced late-peer race proves an older success cannot clear newer uncertainty.

Commit and maintenance: only pre-commit publication participates in capacity retries. Post-commit compaction is isolated and best effort; FULL and other SQLite maintenance failures preserve committed=True and baseline_published=True and do not create corruption markers. Routine compaction requires at least 2 MiB free and at least 25 percent free pages; a 500-test steady-state fixture performs no VACUUM, while a substantially freed store compacts. The quota check is retained as a defensive pre-commit assertion for a widened or changed opener cap, exercised by the practical byte-budget test.

Retention and isolation: candidate time is the only age clock; naive timestamps normalize to UTC. Future timestamps, a guarded datetime.now, and opposite host timezones exercise this contract. Normal-account fixtures wire HOME and pwd lookups to a private account-home, block real-home file/metadata/SQLite access, and guard any integrated platform.domain_paths resolver. Healthy, quota, and corrupt publish paths plus every read helper leave the normal-domain tree unchanged. An AST assertion rejects platform/domain resolver imports. Every read helper now retains one read-only SQLite snapshot, with real peer-write contention proving snapshot consistency and no filesystem mutation.

Remaining regression holes closed: partial non-empty schema reads persist coordinator-corrupt; realistic extended SQLite read-only rollback code 776 and busy-snapshot failures remain per-call unavailability; opaque storage.open_database coordinator-corrupt Problems remain unavailable without permanent markers; every peer schema observation must be complete; older/equal-sequence and scoped passes cannot clear whole-gate obligations across compatibility. Byte-budget fixtures seed a genuine clean full baseline plus failure and whole-gate obligations, publish more than twice the logical budget, and assert non-vacuous oldest-row deletion plus protected evidence survival. Reconciliation rows are count-bounded and expendable under byte pressure, not unconditionally preserved.

Secure-by-spec axes: identity/authentication N/A (no credentials or remote identity are introduced); authorization uses validated owned private paths and the existing forged-checkout regression; tenancy uses explicit domain/checkout isolation; input covers malformed schema, timestamps, and quota; state covers rollback, late peers, immutable receipts and consistent snapshots; exposure keeps canonical public serialization and exact non-sensitive marker fields; availability covers finite eviction, a 2-second lock deadline and relative compaction; dependencies remain local SQLite/filesystem/stdlib, with no new dependency or network path. Additional abuse cases identified during repair were marker allocation failure after FULL, interrupted recovery erasing previous FULL uncertainty, and inconsistent multi-query read snapshots.

Observed initial RED command: scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'capacity or sqlite_full or compaction or steady_state or retention or byte_pruning or opener_corrupt or normal_domain or partial_nonempty or whole_gate_across or transient_read or concurrent_first' --durations=10 -> 9 failed, 16 passed, 36 deselected in 0.64s. Eight failures exposed implementation defects; one was the new test guard incorrectly resolving descriptor-relative paths and was corrected. The same command then passed 25 tests, 36 deselected in 1.10s. Existing correct candidate-clock, partial-schema, whole-gate and extended-code controls are regression coverage, not claimed new RED findings.

Additional commands and evidence: scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'real_sqlite_full or full_recovery_exhausts or capacity_marker_cannot' --durations=5 -> 3 passed, 61 deselected in 0.21s (added after the first implementation; no pre-fix RED claimed). scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'reserved_uncertainty or transient_publish_failure' --durations=5 -> RED 1 failed, 1 passed, 64 deselected in 0.19s. scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'reserved_uncertainty or transient_publish_failure or capacity or compaction or sqlite_full' --durations=5 -> GREEN 10 passed, 56 deselected in 0.28s.

Additional RED/GREEN: scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k every_read_helper_keeps --durations=5 -> RED 3 failed, 66 deselected in 0.39s; GREEN 3 passed, 66 deselected in 0.06s. scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k late_peer --durations=5 -> 1 passed, 69 deselected in 0.18s. scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k interrupted_capacity_recovery --durations=5 -> RED 2 failed, 70 deselected in 0.23s. scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py -k 'interrupted_capacity_recovery or transient_publish_failure' --durations=5 -> GREEN 3 passed, 69 deselected in 0.09s.

Final owned-module command: scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_history.py --durations=10 -> exit 0, 72 passed in 1.72s. Slowest: steady-state inventory 0.36s, substantial freelist 0.14s, each byte-budget fixture 0.13s. No slow test pattern required removal. All tests used the frozen bootstrap dispatcher with local backend and one worker; no raw test runner was invoked.

Other verification: git diff --check -> exit 0; both owned Python files parse with ast.parse. graphify update . -> exit 0, local AST-only rebuild, 3106 nodes / 5648 edges / 219 communities, no semantic extraction or source upload. Read-only local audit-spec review covered the brief, frozen contracts, publication/recovery/read call paths, quota and retention behavior, test sensitivity, and owned-file scope; independent approval is not claimed.
concerns: Independent Opus High audit and the integrated repository-wide final gate remain orchestrator-owned and pending; scripts/ptest-bootstrap intentionally rejects --full.
Bandit, Gitleaks and pip-audit are not installed/configured in this checkout; no scanner or property/fuzz gate is claimed. No dependency or CI changes were authorized.

Linux evidence includes real SQLite page exhaustion and deterministic peer interleavings. Actual hot-journal recovery, kernel ENOSPC/power-loss fault injection, macOS/foreign-UID behavior and stress testing remain unverified. T2 platform.py is absent here; the fixture guards its resolver when integrated, but integrated T2 execution was not tested.
Graphify completed with the existing zero-node warnings for review.json and protocol-v1.json; both owned Python files were included in the refreshed graph.
